issues.summary: healRaiseAlert_ was never refactored onto Step 4's new raiseCalendarAlert_ helper, so it hand-rolls a second calendar path and breaks three of Step 4's own contracts. (a) PROHIBITION VIOLATION: it references CalendarApp.EventColor directly, and step4.md's Prohibitions say verbatim 'Do not reference CalendarApp outside staleness.gs' -- staleness.gs is deliberately the SOLE source of that OAuth scope so a scope change can never take /exec (the only ingest path) down with un-consented code. step4.md's own Verification Procedure #2 ('Confirm by grep that CalendarApp appears in no file other than staleness.gs') demonstrably FAILS today, yet step 4 is marked completed in index.json: `grep -rn CalendarApp connectors/gas/*.gs` returns Code.gs:1958, and git confirms this is a NEW '+' line in this phase. raiseCalendarAlert_ solves this correctly by taking the color as a string KEY and resolving it via stalenessResolveColor_ INSIDE staleness.gs -- healRaiseAlert_ should call it. (b) NO IDEMPOTENCY: raiseCalendarAlert_ dedupes via a getEventsForDay 'titles already on the day' check and returns 0; healRaiseAlert_ has no such check, so every re-run creates ANOTHER all-day event for the same week+kind. healWeeks_ heals up to SUMMARY_HEAL_WEEKS_=4 weeks per run and every greenBeanPull_ override routes through weeklySummarize, so a persistently-drifted week spams a duplicate event per invocation -- on the exact channel meant to signal real corruption. Step 4 wrote a dedicated test for this on its own path ('The alert is idempotent within a day'); the heal path has none. (c) BLOB DESCRIPTION: step4.md requires bodyLines as an ARRAY so 'callers must not hand-build one long blob'; healWeek_ passes alertDetail.join('\n\n') -- one blob.

The new guarded write path silently under-writes a week and can NEVER converge, and the new drift guard then alerts on it forever with no available remediation. Root cause is a normalization mismatch across a boundary this phase made load-bearing: aggregateSupplierRows_ groups on RAW strings (Code.gs:1753, department||kind||name||location, case- and whitespace-sensitive) while rowKey_ normalizes with .trim().toLowerCase(). Two source rows differing only by case/trailing space therefore produce TWO groups but ONE key, and upsertRows_ discards the second as duplicatesSkipped without ever summing it (Code.gs:642). VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY with a probe built from the test_code.js prelude: source rows Mayers/'Leible North'/$100 + 'mayers '/'leible north'/$250 (source total $350) produce 2 groups, 1 distinct rowKey_, and upsertRows_ -> {rowsAdded:1,duplicatesSkipped:1} leaving Summary at $100 -- $250 silently lost. A SECOND heal against that live Summary returns {rowsAdded:0,rowsUpdated:0,duplicatesSkipped:2}: healWeek_ reports action:'heal', rowsUpdated:0, raises no alert and flags no orphan (healOrphanCandidates_ builds computedKeys from the same normalized rows, so both variants collapse to the one live key) -- indistinguishable from 'already correct'. Meanwhile auditSummaryDrift_ (summary_audit.gs:126-140) iterates the recomputed groups and DOES see it: group 1 matches, group 2 hits the same key and pushes a stale entry of {live:100, actual:250}, so checkSummaryDrift raises a calendar alert every Monday, permanently. That is precisely the un-actionable recurring alert Step 4 built the SPLIT-week suppression to avoid, except here the heal claims success. aggregateSupplierRows_/upsertRows_ are both PRE-EXISTING and unmodified by this diff, so this is inherited rather than introduced -- but this phase promotes it from a one-shot summarize bug to a self-heal that re-asserts the understated total across a rolling 4-week window while the new guard alarms on it indefinitely. Fix: group in aggregateSupplierRows_ using the same trim().toLowerCase() normalization rowKey_ uses (or dedupe/sum collisions before the upsert), and treat a non-zero duplicatesSkipped on the heal path as a reportable condition rather than silence.

UNTESTED LOGIC: healRaiseAlert_ has zero test coverage. grep of 'Summary heal|healRaiseAlert|createAllDayEvent' in connectors/gas/test_code.js matches only the CalendarApp mock definition (:245) and one unrelated comment (:7054) -- no test asserts that a heal raises an alert, that a SPLIT-skip/duplicate-refusal of the NEWEST week escalates to RED severity (the isNewest high-severity rule is a stated PRD-12 behaviour), or that a broken calendar does not throw out of it. Step 2 is tdd:true with full red/green evidence, so the gap is enumerated-case coverage, not a skipped test -- the alerting half of the guarded write path simply was not enumerated. By contrast Step 4 wrote 12 cases covering exactly these properties for its own calendar path, which is the standard this should meet.

The new approval-staleness gate fails OPEN on a malformed approval record. 'var stale = !!approved && typeof approved.approvedAt === number && (Date.now() - approved.approvedAt) > MAX_AGE' evaluates to false when approvedAt is missing or non-numeric, so such an approval is treated as FRESH and, if its count+keys still match, authorizes the delete -- the exact bypass the fix was added to close. Low reachability today (runSummaryOrphanSweepDryRun is new and always stamps approvedAt, so no legacy un-stamped property can exist), but the Script Property is hand-editable from the GAS UI and this is a destructive path. Prefer requiring a valid timestamp: treat a missing/non-numeric approvedAt as stale rather than fresh.

healEarliestBackupRows_ is an orphan helper -- no production caller. grep of healEarliestBackupRows_ across connectors/ returns only its own definition, one comment at Code.gs:71, and four test assertions; the repo's only actual restore entry point is mayers.gs:538 restoreMayersLocationSnapshot(). Step 5 documents the 3am rollback as 'data undo is the EARLIEST Summary_heal_backup snapshot per week', and this function encodes exactly that non-obvious earliest-run_id selection -- but an operator has no way to invoke it and must hand-pick rows by run_id in the Sheet under pressure. Note the underlying snapshot-once guarantee IS sound: healWeeks_ (Code.gs:2120-2122) seeds ctx.backedUpWeeks from the existing backup tab, so the guard holds ACROSS runs, not just within one. Consider a zero-arg restoreSummaryHealSnapshot(week) wrapper mirroring the Mayers precedent.
